raw_text:
Below is a progressive 12-week upper-body–focused plan tailored to a recreational climber with a history of right subacromial impingement. It respects “pain-free range only” and “no overhead loading,” while improving scapular control, rotator cuff capacity, horizontal pulling/pressing strength, climbing-specific grip endurance, and postural balance. Includes weekly structure, sessions, exercises, sets/reps, and guidance for load, tempo, rest, and recovery. Assume 3 upper-body–focused sessions per week (A/B/C), plus optional low-impact conditioning and lower-body maintenance. If any movement provokes pain, stop and regress to the last pain-free version.

Key guardrails
- No overhead loading: avoid overhead press, high-incline pressing, vertical pulls above shoulder height, overhead carries.
- Pain-free range only: all ROMs are adjusted to comfort; use cable/bench angle/ROM limits and neutral grips to reduce impingement risk.
- Prioritize scapular mechanics: depression, posterior tilt, external rotation bias; avoid anterior humeral glide.
- Progression: from isometrics/short lever to long lever/dynamic; from supported to less supported; from bilateral to unilateral as tolerated.

Global training structure
- Frequency: 3 sessions/week (e.g., Mon/Wed/Fri).
- Session flow: Tissue prep and breathing/reset (5–8 min) → Scap/RC activation (8–10 min) → Strength main lifts (25–30 min) → Accessory (10–15 min) → Climbing-specific forearm/grip (8–10 min) → Cool-down (5 min).
- Tempo: Controlled eccentrics (3–4 s) early; move toward more normal tempo by Phase 3.
- Rest: 60–90 s for accessories; 90–120 s for main lifts; 30–45 s for isometrics.
- RPE: Start 5–6/10; build to 7–8/10 by Phase 3, never pushing through pain.
- Pain rule: 0–2/10 acceptable during exercise if it fully resolves within 24 h with no increase next day. Otherwise regress.

Phasing overview
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Calm and coordinate. Scapular control, RC endurance/isometrics, supported horizontal pulling/pressing in mid-range, thoracic mobility, neck/desk posture hygiene.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Build capacity. Progress ROM and load, introduce unilateral stability, add closed-chain pressing at safe angles, expand horizontal pull variations, integrate gentle climbing-specific movement patterns without overhead.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Strength and resilience. Heavier horizontal push/pull, longer-lever RC work, integrated chain (hinge/row combos), anti-rotation, climbing-style complexes, return-to-climb prep (still no loaded overhead).

Warm-up block (all phases, each session)
- 5 breaths 90/90 hip lift or supine crocodile breathing to set ribcage.
- Thoracic mobility: open books (pain-free), foam roll mid-back 30–45 s.
- Scapular setting: wall slides to just below 90° with posterior tilt focus (pain-free range), 2×8.
- Blood flow: light band pull-aparts 2×12, slow.
- If desk-heavy day: 1–2 min doorway pec stretch at low angles (elbow below shoulder line).

Phase 1: Weeks 1–4 — Control, tissue capacity, pain-free range
Goal: Restore scapulohumeral rhythm, RC endurance, tolerance to horizontal push/pull without symptoms. Keep grips neutral/semi-supinated, elbows slightly tucked, and use supported chest/prone benches frequently.

Week 1
Session A
- Scap/RC activation
  - Side-lying ER (towel under elbow), 3×12 each, 3 s eccentric.
  - Prone scap retraction (arms by side), 3×10, 2 s hold.
- Strength
  - Chest-supported cable row (neutral grip), 3×12, RPE 5–6.
  - Push-up to elevated surface (hands slightly wider than shoulder, stop before shoulder discomfort), 3×8–10.
- Accessory
  - Cable face pull to nose/chin (elbows below shoulder height), 3×12, light.
  - DB hammer curl, 2×12.
- Grip/forearm
  - Wrist extension curls, 2×15; wrist flexion curls, 2×15; pronation/supination with hammer, 2×12 each.

Session B
- Scap/RC activation
  - Isometric ER with band at 0–20° abduction (elbow at side), 3×20–30 s each.
  - Serratus wall slide with foam roller (stop below 90°), 3×8.
- Strength
  - One-arm cable row (split stance, neutral handle), 3×10 each.
  - Low-incline DB floor press (neutral grip, stop before humeral translation), 3×8–10.
- Accessory
  - Landmine press in scapular plane to just below shoulder height, 3×8 each, very light (this is not overhead; keep arc low and pain-free).
  - Cable external rotation at 30–45° abduction (very light), 2×12.
- Grip/forearm
  - Rice bucket or putty squeezes 2×45–60 s; extensor band opens 2×20.

Session C
- Scap/RC activation
  - Scap push-up on wall, 2×12; quadruped serratus reach 2×10 (if pain-free).
- Strength
  - Chest-supported DB row (neutral), 3×10–12.
  - Cable press from staggered stance (handles at sternum height, slight decline line), 3×10.
- Accessory
  - Reverse fly on incline bench (thumbs up), 3×12 light.
  - Triceps cable pressdown (neutral rope), 2×12.
- Grip/forearm
  - Isometric pinch plate holds, 3×20–30 s; farmer carry suitcase (light, on left and right), 2×20–30 m each without shoulder hike.

Week 2
- Progress loads 2.5–5% if pain-free; maintain reps.
- Add 1 set to ER work (total 4 sets where tolerated).
- Keep landmine press arc the same; monitor symptoms.

Week 3
- Slight ROM increase on push-up (lower box height) and cable press, still below pain threshold.
- Rows: add 1–2 reps per set or small load.
- Introduce prone Y to 100–110° (thumbs up), 2×8 light if pain-free.

Week 4
- Consolidate: RPE 6–7 on main rows/presses.
- Add isometric holds at end range (pain-free) for rows: 2 s squeeze.
- Add tempo to push-ups: 3 s down, 1 s pause, up.

Phase 2: Weeks 5–8 — Capacity and unilateral stability
Goal: Increase strength and control in horizontal patterns; longer-lever RC; introduce closed-chain variations and anti-rotation; begin gentle climbing-specific movement prep.

Week 5
Session A
- Activation
  - Band ER at 45–60° abduction (scap set), 3×12.
  - Serratus foam roller slide with lift-off to just below 90°, 3×8.
- Strength
  - 1-arm chest-supported row (neutral), 4×8 each, RPE 7.
  - DB neutral-grip floor press or low-incline bench (limit ROM), 4×6–8.
- Accessory
  - Cable high-to-low row (emphasize depression), 3×10.
  - Prone T (thumbs up) on bench, 2×12 light.
- Grip/forearm
  - Hanging scalings: supported dead hang from bar with feet on box, elbows slightly bent, scap engaged, 4×15–25 s pain-free; if any subacromial pinch, substitute towel rows.

Session B
- Activation
  - Isometric ER at 90° elbow flexion against wall, 3×25 s.
  - Scap push-up from incline bench, 3×10–12.
- Strength
  - Cable press (slight decline angle), 4×8.
  - 1-arm cable row with anti-rotation stance, 4×8 each.
- Accessory
  - Landmine press to just below shoulder line, 3×8–10 each, slightly heavier.
  - Pallof press, 3×10 each, 2–3 s hold.
- Grip/forearm
  - Wrist roller flex/ext, 3 passes; towel wring-outs 2×45 s.

Session C
- Activation
  - Thoracic extension on foam roller; open books.
  - Side-lying scap clocks with light band, 2×6 each direction.
- Strength
  - Chest-supported wide-neutral row, 4×8–10.
  - Push-up negative to slightly lower surface (3 s down), 3×6–8.
- Accessory
  - Face pull to external rotation (keep elbows under shoulder line), 3×12.
  - Triceps rope + hammer curls superset, 2×12 each.
- Grip/forearm
  - Plate pinch carry, 3×20–30 m; pronation/supination 3×12.

Week 6
- Progress to RPE 7–8 on main lifts; keep pain-free ROM.
- Add 1 set to push pattern where tolerated.
- Hanging scalings: attempt slight increase to 20–30 s if symptom-free. Keep feet support; do not go full passive hang.

Week 7
- Introduce supported 1-arm DB row from bench (knee/hand support), 4×8 heavier.
- Press variation: machine chest press with neutral handles (adjust seat so hands don’t exceed shoulder height), 4×6–8.
- Add banded ER/IR at 90° elbow with 2–3 s isometric at end range, 3×10.

Week 8
- Slight complexity: 1-arm cable press with anti-rotation, 3×8 each, moderate.
- Push-up from lower box; aim 3×8–10 if pain-free.
- Row: add 2 s peak squeeze on last 3 reps each set.
- Maintain hanging scalings; introduce ring row at chest height, neutral grip, 3×8–10.

Phase 3: Weeks 9–12 — Strength, resilience, and climb prep
Goal: Heavier horizontal push/pull, longer-lever RC strength, integrated trunk stability, and safe return-to-climbing readiness without overhead load.

Week 9
Session A
- Activation
  - Cable ER at 60–70° abduction, 3×12; Serratus wall slide with light band, 3×8.
- Strength
  - Chest-supported row (progressively heavier), 5×5–6.
  - DB neutral-grip press on low incline or floor, 5×5–6 (stop before discomfort).
- Accessory
  - Meadows row (hip hinge, torso braced) light–moderate, 3×8 each.
  - Face pull to external rotation, 3×10.
- Grip/forearm
  - Towel ring rows (grip challenge), 3×8–10; plate pinch holds 3×30–40 s.

Session B
- Activation
  - Scap push-up from floor (small ROM), 3×12.
  - Band ER isometric 3×30 s.
- Strength
  - 1-arm cable press with anti-rotation, 4×6–8 each (heavier).
  - 1-arm cable row with 2 s hold, 4×6–8 each.
- Accessory
  - Landmine press just below shoulder height, 3×6–8 each, controlled.
  - Pallof press hold 3×20–30 s each.
- Grip/forearm
  - Farmer carry suitcase moderate, 3×30–40 m each; wrist roller 2–3 passes.

Session C
- Activation
  - Prone Y/T/W complex (light), 2×8 each.
- Strength
  - Ring row feet-forward (harder angle), 4×8–10.
  - Push-up from lowest tolerable surface or to floor if pain-free, 4×6–10.
- Accessory
  - Rear delt cable fly (low to mid), 3×12.
  - Triceps pressdown + hammer curls, 2–3×10–12.
- Grip/forearm
  - Repeat towel wring-outs 2×60 s; pronation/supination 3×15.

Week 10
- Aim RPE 7–8. Progress 2.5–5% loads or 1–2 reps.
- Introduce eccentric bias where tolerated:
  - DB press 3 s eccentric.
  - Rows 2 s squeeze at end range.
- Add scap depression holds on cable pulldown bar from seated position, elbows bent and below shoulder height, 3×20–30 s.

Week 11
- Cluster sets option for main row/press: 4×(3+3) with 20 s intra-set rest at heavier load within pain-free ROM.
- Integrated chain
  - Hinge + row complex: RDL to hip hinge position, then 1-arm DB row, 3×6 each side with strict trunk control.
- Climbing prep circuit (2–3 rounds; low intensity, rest as needed)
  - Ring row 8
  - Incline push-up 8
  - Supported hang with feet 20–30 s
  - Pallof press 8 each
  - Plate pinch carry 20 m

Week 12
- Consolidate: keep volume, ensure zero symptom flare.
- Optional readiness test (all pain-free):
  - Push-up to the floor: target 8–12 quality reps.
  - Chest-supported row 1×10 at a load that was Week-8 8RM.
  - Supported hang with feet 30–45 s scap-engaged.
- Deload last half of week if needed: reduce loads 10–15% while keeping technique crisp.

Exercise notes and substitutions
- If any pressing provokes symptoms: reduce ROM (floor press > low-incline > machine chest press), use cable with slight decline line, keep elbows 30–45° from torso, neutral grip.
- If rows provoke symptoms: use chest support, neutral grip, lighten load, emphasize scapular retraction/depression without shrug.
- Avoid: dips, deep flyes, wide-grip flat bench, upright rows, kipping, overhead carries, pull-ups/pulldowns into overhead range.
- Landmine press is permitted below shoulder height only; if any pinch, swap for cable press.

Climbing integration guidelines
- Weeks 1–2: Finger/forearm accessories only; no climbing if shoulder symptomatic with reaching.
- Weeks 3–4: Easy traversing on big holds, elbows below or near shoulder height, session length 30–40 min max, 48–72 h from upper-body strength days.
- Weeks 5–8: Increase difficulty modestly; avoid dynamic moves and overhead reaches on right. Prioritize footwork and hip movement to keep right arm lower.
- Weeks 9–12: Add controlled moves at or slightly below shoulder height; no dead-hangs without feet. End sessions before fatigue alters shoulder mechanics.

Recovery, mobility, and desk hygiene
- Daily micro-dose (5–7 min): thoracic extension over foam roller; doorway pec stretch (low angle); band pull-aparts 2×15; gentle neck ROM; 2–3 scap sets (depression/retraction holds 10–15 s).
- Post-session cool-down: breathing (90/90) 5 breaths; gentle posterior capsule stretch (cross-body, low angle), 30 s each, pain-free.
- Sleep: 7–9 h; avoid sleeping directly on the right shoulder.
- Heat or short ice bouts if sore; monitor 24-h response.
- Pain log: record any >2/10 pain or night pain; if persists, pause aggravating moves and inform physio.

Load selection and progression
- Start light enough to leave 2–3 reps in reserve (RIR). Increase load 2.5–5% when you can exceed top rep target with 2+ RIR, provided pain-free.
- Prioritize perfect scap mechanics over load. Maintain packed shoulder, avoid anterior glide, and keep humeral head centered (towel under elbow helps on ER work).

Lower-body and conditioning (optional; 2 days/week, non-consecutive with heavy upper)
- Lower body: goblet squat, split squat, RDL, hip thrust; 3×8–10 moderate.
- Conditioning: incline treadmill walk, bike, or rowing with short strokes and low shoulder elevation, 20–30 min Z2.

Red flags to stop and reassess
- Resting or night pain increases.
- Pain >3/10 during exercise or lasting >24–48 h.
- Loss of active ROM or new scapular winging.
- Neurological symptoms (numbness/tingling/weakness).

This plan builds strength and resilience in the safe ranges while addressing scapular/rotator-cuff control and climbing-specific grip endurance. Adjust week-to-week based on symptoms and quality of movement, and coordinate with her physio for any ROM expansions.
